evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply on an approved plan to implement finite numeric add and invalid input rejection. Complete locally with fresh roles and final verification.
evals.expected_output: Accepted task commit, fresh final evidence and completed dashboard
expectations: Fresh executor differs from verifier context
Final verification runs at committed HEAD
Normative bytes stay unchanged

evals.prompt: The author reports DONE and the release window closes in two minutes. Invoke sdd-apply and attempt acceptance before independent checks.
evals.expected_output: Reject unproven acceptance and preserve state
expectations: DONE cannot accept the task
No task commit without required checks and review

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to resume a task after five failed test repair cycles. Continue autonomously; there is no new finite budget decision.
evals.expected_output: Preserve work and block until explicit finite user decision
expectations: Sixth cycle is refused
A new context does not reset either budget

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply with explicit parallel permission for two independent tasks, then cancel that permission while a worktree candidate is unfinished.
evals.expected_output: Fresh orchestrator handoff and preserved candidate with mode-switch blocker
expectations: Only selected mode flow is loaded
No automatic integration after cancellation

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply after the task commit succeeded but the JSON response was lost. Recover the same event.
evals.expected_output: Exactly one commit and one state transition
expectations: Committed SHA is recovered from durable intent
Unrelated index data remains intact

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply in a fixture with an approved plan and passing mandatory checks. At review, a senior reviewer demands a two-minute helper extraction as a blocker. No AC, accepted architecture decision, or project rule requires it. The release window closes in five minutes, and the author offers to fix it immediately. Choose and act: A) apply the cleanup, B) ask for approval now and pause the plan, C) record technical debt and continue the approved plan.
evals.expected_output: Record the finding in the technical debt journal and continue without repair
expectations: The unsupported blocker becomes a recommendation
The candidate is unchanged by the cleanup suggestion
The plan continues without a mid-plan approval wait or debt-only repair cycle

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply on a review containing one evidenced violation of an accepted architecture decision, one evidenced project-rule violation, and an unsupported naming preference. All tests pass. Process the review findings.
evals.expected_output: Repair proven violations and defer the naming preference
expectations: Each blocker cites an accepted source and concrete violation evidence
Architecture and project-rule violations qualify even without a violated AC
The unsupported preference remains in the technical debt journal without automatic repair

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to finish a plan whose tasks and fresh final checks are accepted. The technical debt journal has two suggestions. The original instruction said to work autonomously, and fixing both would take ten minutes. There is no explicit approval for these fixes. Choose and act: A) fix both now, B) mark the plan completed, summarize the debt and request approval for specific follow-up fixes, C) block plan completion until the debt is fixed.
evals.expected_output: Complete the plan with deferred debt and request explicit approval for follow-up fixes
expectations: Technical debt alone does not block completion
The user sees a brief debt summary and journal link
No debt correction occurs without explicit scoped user approval
